clue.text: Has groom seen the settlement? Itês attractive

indicators.note: a settlement is something sorted out and arranged, so the preceding words are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A curious question about whether a stable lad has witnessed some settlement, followed by a remark that it is attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: The four words before 'settlement' rearrange to HORSESHOE MAGNET; the odd 'Itês' is the website's mangling of 'It's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-shaped magnet pulls iron towards it, so it is literally something that attracts metal objects.

clue.text: Hoarding money retains German approval. That's touching!

indicators.note: to retain is to hold on to, so the earlier words wrap around what follows

blocks.note: a hoarding is a billboard carrying an advertisement, an ad

explanation.surface: A billboard firm keeps hold of German endorsement, and somebody is moved by it.
explanation.walkthrough: A hoarding is the British word for a billboard. The money piece and the advert piece together wrap around the German.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are adjacent lie next to each other, in contact, so the exclamation stands for the adjective.

clue.text: British invader losing time in conflict

indicators.note: losing something means it drops out, so a letter is removed from the word for conflict

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a tangle is a dispute or fight

explanation.surface: An invader of Britain loses ground over time in a war.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the T off TANGLE to leave ANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angles were a Germanic people who settled in Britain after the Romans left, giving England its name.

clue.text: Bird of prey makes novelist cry

blocks.note: C. P. Snow was an English novelist
a yowl is a loud wailing cry

explanation.surface: A predatory bird reduces an author to tears.
explanation.definitionFit: This large white Arctic owl hunts lemmings and other small animals, so it is a raptor.

clue.text: Private is accepted within group of players

definitions.note: plural for a singular noun: the septet is the seven players together

indicators.note: being accepted within a group means going inside it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: Pte is the army abbreviation for the rank of private

explanation.surface: A private soldier is welcomed into a band of musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group of players' reads as one phrase, but 'group' supplies the wordplay and 'players' alone is the definition, joined by 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A septet is a band of seven musicians, so it is a company of performers taken together.

clue.text: Lubricant for first woman MP squeezed by snake

indicators.note: something squeezed by another is held tightly inside it

blocks.note: Nancy Astor was the first woman to take her seat in the House of Commons
to snake is to coil, or a coil is a snake's winding

explanation.surface: A pioneering female politician is crushed by a serpent, needing something to ease her escape.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy Astor, elected in 1919, was the first woman to sit in the House of Commons, a fact crossword setters lean on often.
explanation.definitionFit: The oil pressed from castor beans was long used to grease machinery as well as a laxative.

clue.text: Hold sailor's globe

blocks.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor; with the possessive it gives AB'S

explanation.surface: A seaman's globe is a thing to hang on to.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb is to take in and retain, as a sponge holds water.

clue.text: One prone to stoop finds variety of grape in Florence

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so the letters are made into a different form

explanation.surface: Someone with a bad posture discovers a new grape in an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stoop' sounds like poor posture, but a falcon's stoop is its steep dive onto prey.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is famous for its high-speed plunge, called a stoop, so it habitually dives on its quarry.

clue.text: Bill or Bob keeps batting

indicators.note: to keep is to hold within, so the dance word surrounds the cricket term

blocks.note: to bob is to move up and down, to dance
a batsman in cricket is said to be in

explanation.surface: Two men's names, Bill or Bob, with one of them at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' and 'Bob' look like a pair of names; Bill is the definition, a draft law.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a draft law, and an ordinance is an authoritative decree or local by-law.

clue.text: Walk accomplished around Maidenhead

indicators.note: around means one word goes round the outside of another

blocks.note: read as maiden's head, the first letter of maiden; M is also the cricket scoring abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A capable stroll round the Thames town of Maidenhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Maidenhead is a town in Berkshire, but the clue splits it into 'Maiden' and 'head'.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to stroll at a gentle, unhurried pace.

clue.text: Martin is reluctant to accept regressive legislation

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse
accepting something means taking it inside

blocks.note: slow to do something is reluctant

explanation.surface: A man named Martin hesitates to back backward-looking laws.
explanation.walkthrough: Martin looks like a man's name, but a martin is a bird. SLOW takes in WAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Martins belong to the swallow family of birds, so the definition gives a close relative as an example.

clue.text: Electronic unit to deter corruption

indicators.note: corruption spoils the original form, so the letters are altered into another order

explanation.surface: A piece of electronics designed to discourage bribery.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrode is a vacuum valve with four electrodes, a component in old electronic circuits.

clue.text: A building in Slough

blocks.note: first meaning: a simple hut or outbuilding
second meaning: to cast off, as a snake does its skin

explanation.surface: Pointing to a building in the town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, but here it is the verb meaning to cast off skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a garden hut and a verb for casting off skin or leaves.

clue.text: Snooker players stop in Hertfordshire?

definitions.note: a place in Hertfordshire, by example

explanation.surface: Snooker players halt somewhere in the Home Counties.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals a definition by example: Potters Bar is a town in Hertfordshire, a county just north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Potters Bar is a commuter town located in that county north of London, so it is one place there.

clue.text: Type of fungus strengthens wood

blocks.note: to beef up is to strengthen

explanation.surface: A kind of fungus reinforces timber.
explanation.definitionFit: The beefsteak fungus is a red bracket that grows on oak trees and looks like raw meat.

clue.text: Ersatz meat loaf endlessly cooked for breakfast

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is dropped
ersatz means imitation, so the letters are made into a fake version of themselves

explanation.surface: A substitute meat loaf, not quite finished, is served up in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the F from LOAF, then rearrange MEAT LOA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground oats are boiled into porridge, a hot morning meal, so they are prepared for the first meal of the day.

clue.text: Shine having knowledge about table

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the knowledge word is placed around the other

explanation.surface: Polishing a table takes some know-how.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is informal British slang for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: To glisten is to sparkle or gleam, the way a wet surface catches light.

clue.text: Cooper bears cost of lexicon

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so the actor's name carries the other word within

blocks.note: Gary Cooper was the Hollywood star of High Noon

explanation.surface: A barrel-maker pays for a dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: A cooper is a barrel-maker, but here it is the film star. GARY holds LOSS.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossary is a list of specialist words with their meanings, a small dictionary.

clue.text: Rip parachute revealing well of emotion

explanation.surface: A torn parachute leaves the skydiver overwhelmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like a noun for a source, but here it hints at a tear that wells up.
explanation.definitionFit: A single tear welling from the eye is an outward sign of sadness or joy.

clue.text: He's an influence for a criminal

explanation.surface: A man who has a bad effect on a lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of He's counts as 'is', joining he to the influence.
explanation.definitionFit: A malefactor is a wrongdoer, someone who commits a crime.

clue.text: Drink when touring a circle of wagons

indicators.note: touring is going round, so the drink goes round the single letter

explanation.surface: Having a beer while travelling in a wagon train.
explanation.definitionFit: A laager is a defensive camp formed by drawing wagons into a ring, from Afrikaans.

clue.text: Metal provides revolutionary casing for digital memory

indicators.note: a casing encloses whatever is put in it

blocks.note: ROM is read-only memory in computing

explanation.surface: Metal makes a radical housing for a computer's memory chip.
explanation.walkthrough: Che Guevara is the crossword's stock revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Chrome is chromium, the shiny metallic element used for plating.

clue.text: It can be blown indiscreetly, producing a boom

blocks.note: first meaning: to blow the ... is to give away a secret
second meaning: a spar on a sailing ship holding the top of a sail

explanation.surface: Something blown carelessly makes a loud bang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blown' and 'boom' suggest an explosion; the idiom 'blow the gaff' means to reveal a secret.
explanation.definitionFit: The word completes the idiom for letting out a secret, and also names a nautical spar like a boom.

clue.text: Gas creates fuss among sailors

indicators.note: among means in the middle of, so one word is placed inside the other

explanation.surface: Talk among sailors stirs up a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a radioactive noble element that exists as a vapour at room temperature.

clue.text: A good supporter works hard

definitions.note: verb phrase for a noun: one who works hard

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a rafter is a beam supporting a roof

explanation.surface: A loyal fan puts in a lot of effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' looks like a fan, but it is a roof beam. Read cryptically: a G plus RAFTER is someone who works hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Grafter is British slang for a diligent person, from graft meaning hard labour.

clue.text: Boy returns after examination in disgrace

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A lad comes back after a test result, shamed.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is a shameful public affair that brings disrepute.

clue.text: Medical procedure shown in hygiene manual

indicators.note: shown in means the letters are on display inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A clinical technique described in a cleanliness handbook.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema is the injection of fluid into the bowel, a treatment carried out by medical staff.

clue.text: Merchant and traveller displays the spirit o' the game

blocks.note: marc is a brandy distilled from grape residue
polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: A trader and explorer shows sporting enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit of the game' looks like sporting attitude, but the spirit is a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The thirteenth-century Venetian trader journeyed to China and wrote of his travels.
